assessment: Extubation and dysphonia were managed through DBS programming. Swallowing features are clinical context and no food test is reported.
Dysarthria and related symptoms occur in a case diagnosed as MSA-C. No dietary exposure or swallowing intervention was compared.
A prescribing care plan addressed timely medication delivery, including when swallowing is difficult. No ingredient or swallowing result was estimated.
FIBER-MED includes kiwi, prunes, hydration and additional care. The program shows within-person bowel changes. Individual food effects remain unmeasured.
Feeding was an activity impaired by essential tremor. Some diagnoses changed on follow-up. Food intake and symptom response were unavailable.
Peach is a cited author's surname. The study compares DBS contact selection.
Fiber photometry measures neural activity in a dyskinesia model. No dietary fiber exposure was tested.
Fecal biomarkers were used to classify young-onset parkinsonism. Fatty acids occur in cited microbiome literature. The comparison did not administer food.
Salmon is a cited author's surname. The poster concerns a diagnostic acrostic.
A dietary cognition study appears in the references. The MemHiN abstract concerns neurogenesis markers and cognitive and neuropsychiatric testing.
An Aerva lanata decoction was tested in flies. This botanical is outside the frozen ingredient set.
Dysphagia is one planned symptom variable in the AI-PMP protocol. No food exposure is specified.
The diet and microbiome cohort reports associations with diagnostic and prodromal groups. Separate preparation-specific symptom estimates are unavailable.
Apple refers to the Apple Watch. The poster concerns wearable motor assessment.
The authors identified abetalipoproteinemia. Dietary management and swallowing context concern that condition.
The primary case is cerebellar ischemic stroke and hemifacial spasm. The study has no food intervention or Parkinson cohort.
Speech and related symptoms were classified in confirmed MSA and PSP. The abstract reports no food exposure.
A Parkinson dysphagia questionnaire was compared with caregiver ratings. The abstract gives no food-specific response.
Mixed neurological and healthy participants attended courses that included nutrition. Aggregate perceptions and attendance are reported without ingredient-specific outcomes.
The Chonnam report relates reported coffee intake to selected executive tests. It gives no separate fatigue estimate or brewing details.
Stroke-cohort incidence and motor severity analyses use circulating IL-6 and lipoprotein(a). Food intake was outside the analysis.
Group telerehabilitation participation was compared on quality of life. No food bolus or dietary intervention was reported.
Leber hereditary optic neuropathy explains the family presentation. The report gives no dietary Parkinson comparison.
Endoscopy in PSP and MSA compares broad liquids and semisolids. The abstract gives no ingredient-specific result in idiopathic Parkinson disease.
Dysphagia and other symptoms occur in a genetically confirmed early Alzheimer case with dystonia. The treatment exposure was clinical medication.
A ketogenic diet is mentioned in a GLUT1 deficiency case. The report supplies no Parkinson symptom comparison.
Fibres refer to neural pathways in a study of DBS and bradykinesia.
Caffeine occurs in a citation on ADCY5-related dyskinesia. The mouse characterization did not test caffeine or brewed coffee.
Tremor is attributed to a spinal schwannoma and resolved after surgery. No culinary exposure was tested.
Orange refers to Agent Orange. The study concerns seizures and parkinsonism.
Binge eating and feeding dystonia are symptoms of chorea-acanthocytosis in this report. No diet–symptom effect was tested.
Apomorphine treatment was followed by motor complication and serum vitamin changes. No food intake or ingredient effect was measured.
Fasting and glucose challenge measurements concern spinocerebellar ataxia type 2. There is no Parkinson food–symptom comparison.
Botulinum toxin was the exposure in patients with head and neck dystonia. Swallowing concerns do not provide food comparisons.
Current aggregate caffeine use was associated with higher dyskinesia severity. Coffee and tea prevalence analyses were inconclusive. Preparation and product-specific severity are unavailable.
Voice therapy was followed by changes in swallowing questionnaire scores. The original figure mentions choking without naming a food.
The randomized comparison tested cannabis extract in a shared MCT carrier. The pain contrast was inconclusive and the carrier effect was not isolated.
The case concerns cerebellar PSP with liquid dysphagia. No Parkinson food effect was tested.
Sialorrhea, autonomic symptoms and swallowing questionnaire scores were clustered in Parkinson disease. No dietary ingredient was assessed.
The study compares tremor and daily activity impairment in multiple sclerosis. No food intervention or Parkinson symptom outcome is reported.
EGG means electrogastrography. The abstract reports ultrasound gastric emptying and subsequent motor activities, with no stated egg meal.
Functional oral intake and dysphagia were compared in MSA. Food-specific Parkinson outcomes were outside the study.
Swallowing questionnaire responses were included among predictors of hospitalization. There is no food-specific exposure or response.
The forest plot includes the 2024 Iranian randomized nicotine-rich diet as one study, alongside drug and patch trials. The aggregate comparison provides no ingredient-specific result.
Turkey identifies the country in an essential tremor thalamotomy study.
The Malaysia cohort reports dysphagia differences across MSA groups. No food-specific Parkinson estimate is available.
Swallowing and choking are questionnaire outcomes in PSP. No food exposure was compared.
Orange refers to Agent Orange exposure in veterans with essential tremor.
Caffeine and tea were included among UK Biobank exposures. The reported estimates concern Parkinson diagnosis and genetic susceptibility, without specific beverage or symptom results.
The oral assessment reports chewing and swallowing concerns and drooling in Parkinson disease. Food residue appears as clinical context, without a named preparation or food comparison.
Cortical activation and airway invasion were evaluated in MSA during swallowing. The report gives no Parkinson food contrast.
The seven-person Mexican cohort reports nutrient-level correlations with motor scores. No individual food or controlled intake comparison is available.
BASIL is a cerebral perfusion analysis toolbox. The study has no herb intake comparison.
Fiber photometry measures neural activity in a Parkinson model. No dietary fiber was administered.
The family report relates dysphagia and voice symptoms to a DCTN1 variant. There is no food intervention.
Urinary metabolites are compared by Parkinson status. Small nerve fiber pathology is mentioned in background.
Aspiration pneumonia occurred during rapidly progressive treatment-associated parkinsonism. No food or obstructing material was identified.
Fiber filtering refers to DBS tractography. The report supplies no dietary exposure.
Nutrition is a planned tracking area in a rehabilitation platform. No clinical dietary outcome is reported.
The PRISM clinic reports utilization and timing of swallowing and GI tests. No food was compared.
The Egypt report compares nutrient intake, overall diet quality and symptom prevalence by diagnosis. Item-specific Parkinson symptom estimates are unavailable.
The Ghosh report links reported meat and milk intake to mortality. The 2025 and 2026 reports share group sizes and comparisons. No symptom estimate is reported.
The gene expression comparison includes nutritional status correlations. No named food is analyzed.
Dorsal DBS contact case series describes anatomical fibre tracts and stimulation effects. No food exposure is compared.
Post-COVID secondary choreodystonia DBS case cites anatomical fibre tracts. No culinary exposure or food-specific outcome is reported.
Fasting glucose and HbA1c are metabolic biomarkers in a glymphatic MRI study. No intake or culinary intervention is estimated.
22q11.2 deletion-associated parkinsonism case presents a diagnostic workup and drug challenge. No ingredient exposure is compared.
Complement prunes inhibitory synapses in the postmortem model. The abstract uses prunes as a verb and evaluates no fruit exposure.

MDS 943, Kakde et al. Respiratory biomarkers and dysphagia systematic review. Both attachments list respiratory tests or screening associations and give no identified food, bolus preparation, ingredient comparison or treatment outcome. Table 1 gives author surnames without years or identifiers, and the readily identifiable 58-person Pitts Chest study differs from its 61-person row, so the table is a lead rather than a verified primary citation.

MDS 139, Wang et al. PSP-only cohort, with penetration or aspiration in 41/62 and oropharyngeal freezing in 6/62. The three tables and figure contain no named food or bolus. The fNIRS subset is eight, with one freezing case. Table 3 gives negative correlations with total dysphagia scores. The cited 2020 Labeit idiopathic PD series is separate.

MDS 1631, Zashchypas and Lorenzl. Proposed n=50 Parkinson cohort with individualized IDDSI texture changes, intake/hydration diaries, FOIS and instrumental outcomes. Abstract supplies no named food, diary data, comparison or observed outcome. Existing contextual note: research/2025-2029/Food-Experiment-Choking-Followup.md#swallowing-concerns-and-diet-records-at-the-2026-mds-congress.

MDS 747, Nakamori et al. 25-person age subgroup of jRCTs062220013. Primary DOI 10.1155/ane/8838225 confirms 3 mL water with 30% barium for VF and inhaled 1% citric acid for cough provocation. Baseline penetration/aspiration was 3/9 vs 7/16 by age (p=.610); electrical stimulation was the intervention. Existing note: research/2025-2029/Food-Experiment-Choking-Followup.md#age-subgroup-of-the-hiroshima-water-bolus-cohort.

MDS 1599, Shah et al. Multilingual surveys and a focus group shaped a nutrition coaching pilot, with preparation, access, dysphagia and cultural preferences reported as barriers. No completed dietary intervention, named food exposure, participant count or clinical outcomes. Separate Columbia Engage-PD source is physical activity coaching. Local note: research/2025-2029/Food-Experiment-MDS-Diet-Followup.md#community-design-of-the-engage-in-healthy-eating-program.

MDS 1037, Leung and Appel-Cresswell. BMRR and VPRI observational cohorts plus the ongoing 12-week UBC ProD powder RCT NCT05568498. Its primary depression and secondary cognition/fatigue scales match, but the poster reports expected directions without observed numbers or treatment-arm results. 2025 BMRR Table 1 has 14 Parkinson diagnoses among 47 baseline visits, no food associations or overlap counts. Separate published TAP trial NCT03968133, PMID 42034654, adds actual fatigue, anxiety and MoCA results for probiotic powder only. Local note: research/2025-2029/Food-Experiment-MDS-Diet-Followup.md#vancouver-probiotic-powder-trials-and-symptom-outcomes.

MDS 1635, Meyer et al. Same 1519-person PREDICT-PD diagnostic odor study as WPC P38.06. Parkinson disease, RBD and pure autonomic failure were excluded. Cinnamon, watermelon and lemon were identification stimuli without ingestion. Already cataloged in research/2025-2029/Food-Experiment-Food-Followup.md#cinnamon-as-a-diagnostic-odor-in-predict-pd.
Food-related paranoid thoughts are psychiatric symptoms in a drug-induced akathisia case. No Parkinson diagnosis or dietary exposure is evaluated.
Swallowing ability worsened in a case of MYORG-related basal ganglia calcification. No bolus, ingredient or dietary treatment is reported.
The video classifier uses standardized MDS-UPDRS hand movements to estimate motor severity. No ingredient or intake comparison appears.
Beta denotes a frequency band in recordings during DBS implantation. The Parkinson hemidystonia comparison measured neuronal activity without a food exposure.
The albumin ratio normalizes cerebrospinal-fluid and serum IgG measurements. No dietary protein or food exposure is estimated.

MDS 183, Karagoz et al. Baseline PROSPECT-M-UK analysis of 164 participants with multiple system atrophy, with 66 matched disease/quality-of-life records. Difficulty swallowing food and drinking fluids were questionnaire items. No identified food, treatment, bolus or idiopathic Parkinson comparison.

MDS 368, Antigua-Matos et al. Adult GNAO1-related dystonia case describes feeding dependence and improved dystonia after pallidal DBS. No named food, objective swallowing result or Parkinson diagnosis.

MDS 709, Bergmans et al. Seven-year incobotulinumtoxinA interim report in 35 advanced Parkinson patients recorded transient swallowing difficulty during 24/208 injection cycles, with no food identified. The 2025 six-year report covers the same 35-patient cohort. Injection was the exposure and the denominator was treatment cycles.

MDS 522, Sharma et al. Single AFG3L2-related late-onset bulbar disorder case with progressive dysarthria and dysphagia. No named food, tested bolus or measured response. The case is outside idiopathic Parkinson disease.

MDS 1296, Hayasaka et al. In 14 patients, continuous levodopa delivery (n=4) showed declining tongue-pressure waveform area over 20 repetitions at 10-second intervals versus intermittent dosing (n=10). This is tongue-force measurement timing, with no meal timing, food bolus, swallowing outcome or significant peak-pressure interaction.

MDS 169, Parmera et al. Coffee intake is reported in 86.4% of an assessed subgroup in the Latin American progressive supranuclear palsy consortium. Figure 1 shows clinical phenotype counts. No preparation, dose, coffee-to-symptom association, or idiopathic Parkinson disease results.

MDS 607, Sarac et al. Two sisters with CCDC88C-associated spastic paraparesis/ataxia had dysphagia. The case series provides no named food, swallowing assessment linked to exposure, or idiopathic Parkinson diagnosis.

MDS 1417, Zaripova et al. ATP13A2-associated Kufor–Rakeb case reports chewing and swallowing trouble from age 21, with improvement under dopaminergic drugs described generally. No food identity, instrumental swallow measure or swallowing-specific treatment response.

MDS 244, Shah et al. Autopsy-confirmed progressive supranuclear palsy case includes dysphagia among background symptoms. Amantadine withdrawal and re-challenge tracked pseudobulbar affect. No named food, tested bolus or swallowing change was reported.

MDS 1896, Rekik et al., 62 Parkinson participants. Cups per day of unspecified caffeine were associated with cognition and levodopa response, and with tremor-dominant subtype but no rest-tremor score or fatigue estimate. No specific preparation. Existing research/2025-2029/Food-Experiment-MDS-Beverage-Followup.md#reported-caffeine-and-nonmotor-symptoms-in-sousse.

MDS 1110, Guo and Li. Genetically predicted tofu intake and diagnosis OR 0.86 (95% CI 0.65 to 1.15), without preparation or drooling outcome. Existing research/2025-2029/Food-Experiment-MDS-Diet-Followup.md#tofu-intake-and-parkinsons-diagnosis.

MDS 826, Fornari Caprara et al. Pooled five diet comparisons in Figure 1, with MDS-UPDRS III MD 0.97 (95% CI −1.99 to 3.92). The Part II figure has four inputs and MD −1.45 (−3.12 to 0.23). Fatigue and dizziness are adverse events with wide uncertainty. The review does not isolate a culinary ingredient. Primary trial tracing follows the figure labels Phillips, Krikorian, Tidman, Worster, and Choi.

MDS 1135, Bestoso et al., 34 Parkinson participants. 41.2% reported a diet change, usually Mediterranean or protein-adjusted. The p=.01 perceived quality-of-life association is for emotional coping. No reported estimate for either diet, named foods, or any specific symptom.

MDS 1326, Zhang et al., 689 NHS and 755 HPFS participants with Parkinson. No clear total caffeine association. Multivitamin RR 0.65 (95% CI 0.52 to 0.82) is for subjective cognitive decline. MIND dietary adherence was modeled but the abstract gives no estimate. Existing research/2025-2029/Food-Experiment-MDS-Beverage-Followup.md#prediagnostic-caffeine-and-later-outcomes-in-two-us-cohorts.

MDS 1233, Sánchez-Ramírez et al., ReMePARK 260 Parkinson participants and 742 observations. Measured weight and BMI change against clinical progression and quality of life. No dietary exposure or intake contrast.

MDS 991, Moya-Salazar et al., 90 Parkinson participants. Fasting serum hepatic markers contrasted across Hoehn and Yahr stages, with direct bilirubin p=.020. No dietary intake or administration, and no symptom-specific comparison.
MDS 1219, Peball et al., 543 Parkinson participants. Symptoms including dysphagia and constipation compared by interest in trials, without food or dietary intervention.
MDS 957, PPMI n=279. Serum and cerebrospinal-fluid biomarker clusters compared for motor and nonmotor progression. No dietary exposure; panel figures address the biomarker and outcome comparisons.

Sukmueng et al. Table 1 identifies pharmaceutical butylphthalide, formulated curcumin, ground soybeans plus levodopa and other previously traced preparations. No new clinical cohort or culinary turmeric/celery comparison. Local note: research/2025-2029/Food-Experiment-MDS-Botanical-Followup.md#herbal-review-table-and-original-preparations.

Surbakti et al. modeled reported Dayak onion constituents without biological exposure or symptom outcomes. Eleutherine naming differs from culinary Allium cepa in 0024/0683. Habibah 2026 LC–MS and Han 2008 isolation confirm related chemical classes, while the poster omits exact compound identifiers. Local note: research/2025-2029/Food-Experiment-MDS-Botanical-Followup.md#dayak-onion-docking-and-bulb-chemistry.

Rajput and Sharma tested intranasal isolated berberine nanoparticles in intracerebroventricular streptozotocin Wistar rats modeling Alzheimer disease. Cognitive maze and biochemical findings do not include Parkinson symptom, culinary ingredient or named carrier evidence. Distinct from Khatri Parkinson model record 35399.

Tsao et al. oral Lactobacillus reuteri Y7 in 6-OHDA rats, with motor and fecal measures. Related patent family CN121818719A/US20260102444A1 and MDS 37064 may share cohorts. NCT07619560 has no human results. No kefir or yogurt exposure. Local note: research/2025-2029/Food-Experiment-MDS-Botanical-Followup.md#probiotic-y7-and-a-medical-food-in-rat-models.

Tang et al. Fig. 1 and sponsor HKEX report show healthy-volunteer relative bioavailability of 118% versus fasting oral tablets and 98.3% versus fed oral tablets. Ingredients and spray enhancer are undisclosed. Related Novaken levodopa patent does not identify the clinical formulation. NCT07156773/CTR20253290 Phase II has no posted results. Local note: research/2025-2029/Food-Experiment-MDS-Botanical-Followup.md#xjn010-nasal-spray-and-fed-oral-comparator.
The stakeholder music-therapy survey discusses speech and swallowing as possible uses. It did not administer music or compare a food exposure.

Cinnamon and other odorants were used to measure odor recognition in early-onset Parkinson disease. The duration comparison is cross-sectional and provides no culinary cinnamon intervention or intake estimate.
The multidisciplinary care review mentions swallowing therapy. The abstract supplies no named bolus or diet-specific Parkinson result.
Apple Watch devices measured mobility in Parkinson caregiver dyads. Apple is the device brand.
Apple Podcasts is a platform in the educational survey. No participant exposure or symptom outcome involves the fruit.
Peach is an author surname in a cited DBS study. The presentation compares stimulation and recorded activity in dystonia.
Food is the semantic verbal-fluency category in Huntington disease. The questionnaire did not measure diet.
A dietitian is part of a supportive-care team. The study compares palliative-care access and outcomes without food or nutrition data.
Dysphagia is a comorbidity in the atypical parkinsonism records. No assigned or measured dietary exposures are reported.
MDS 543 is a VPS13A disease family case series. Dysphagia appears in two case histories. No food, bolus, swallowing test, or idiopathic Parkinson cohort is reported.

MDS 882 reports an online clinician survey and Delphi consensus on PSP and corticobasal syndrome. The table lists generic fiber for constipation. The report supplies no defined fiber preparation or dose, named food, swallowing test, or measured food effect.

MDS 1968 measures progression in 15 participants with type I sialidosis using electrophysiology and ophthalmic assessments. No named food, swallowing outcome, or idiopathic Parkinson cohort is reported.

MDS 1785 evaluates acoustic speech during deep brain stimulation in 25 Parkinson participants. Tasks include reading, phonation and diadochokinesis. No food, meal, or swallowing challenge is reported.

MDS 1927 reports longitudinal ataxia assessments in adults with ataxia-telangiectasia. The attached trajectories show ataxia severity. No named food, measured swallowing outcome, or idiopathic Parkinson cohort is reported.

MDS 359 screened 30 participants with X-linked dystonia-parkinsonism. Table 1 lists 19 genetically confirmed and 11 clinically diagnosed or pending. Twenty-four screened positive for dysphagia risk. Table 3 gives p=.6940 for dysphagia risk by nutrition status. No named food or bolus is reported.

MDS 1851 uses the five-item Oral Frailty Index in 96 older participants with Parkinson disease. Thirty-three reported swallowing difficulty. No administered bolus, measured named-food exposure, or food-specific response is reported.

MDS 236 reports one PSP case evolving from nonfluent primary progressive aphasia. Rocket sign is a neurological exam finding and accounts for the arugula match. The report gives no food exposure or comparison.

MDS 1273 assessed 28 Parkinson participants at home in Tanzania. A 150 mL plain-water screen produced cough or wet voice in 5/10 with cough peak flow below 160 L/min and 0/17 above the threshold in the reported groups (p=.003). No instrumental confirmation, solid-food challenge, or dietary comparison is reported. See research/2025-2029/Food-Experiment-Choking-Followup.md#water-swallow-screening-in-northern-tanzania.

MDS 171 is a surgical retrospective in 202 people with multiple system atrophy, comparing survival by gastrostomy and airway procedure. No feeding formula, ingredient, food exposure, or swallowing response is reported.

This archive record tracks time to dysphagia by REM sleep behavior questionnaire severity in 189 participants with multiple system atrophy. Its figures show progression endpoints. No administered food, bolus, measured dietary exposure, or idiopathic Parkinson cohort is reported.

Cross-sectional 229 Parkinson patients. Metabolic syndrome was more prevalent with higher Hoehn and Yahr stage (38/41 at stages 3 and above vs 79/188 at stage 2 and below by NCEP), with no association with motor onset phenotype. The exposures are glucose, HDL, blood pressure and BMI, without food intake.

PPMI analysis of 154 people with Parkinson’s. The syndrome composite had no clinical association; exploratory results for circulating triglycerides and fasting glucose relate to motor severity and MoCA, respectively. Serum markers do not specify diet or a food.

Exploratory cohort of 54 Parkinson patients. Tyrosine and formate distinguished greater symptom burden, and serum fatty acids, glycerol, citrate and sugars distinguished a lower-burden profile. No intake comparison or identified dietary source.

Longitudinal motor trajectory in 1,042 people with Parkinson’s. Inverted BMI is one element of a frailty score that also includes sleep and fatigue. No food intake, defined dietary intervention or food-by-symptom comparison.

Review of 200 supportive-care encounters, 51 involving nutrition or food concerns. Constipation, swallowing, meal access, weight loss and general inquiry are visit domains. Swallowing is more frequently documented in atypical parkinsonism. No named food or intervention; see research/2025-2029/Food-Experiment-Choking-Followup.md#swallowing-concerns-and-diet-records-at-the-2026-mds-congress.

Prospective 63-person DBS or levodopa cohort. MNA, weight, albumin, vitamins B6/B12 and homocysteine are nutritional status or blood measures; the abstract does not identify a consumed food or clinical effect of dietary change. Treatment is the comparative intervention.

In 37 people with Parkinson’s, MNA-classified malnutrition risk was associated with depression, dysphagia and dyskinesia, and correlated with UPDRS II (rho .338, p .041). Constipation and sialorrhea were also assessed. No food-by-symptom comparison.

MDS 1387 Barichella et al. of 54 discordant pairs. Food contrasts compare Parkinson status; constipation is a separate case-control comparison. Same cohort as full paper in research/2025-2029/Food-Experiment-Food-Followup.md#preserved-fish-and-fruit-frequency-in-parkinson-discordant-twins, including the printed preserved fish discrepancy and 78-food correction.

Gastric electrogastrography, ultrasound, and neuroimaging in 56 early Parkinson patients and 26 controls. Objective gastric motility group is the comparison. Abstract provides no dietary exposure or ingredient contrast; underlying methods can clarify any standardized test meal.
Thai cross-sectional cohort of 124. Sarcopenia was associated with Parkinson severity and weight change, with no food intake or nutrition treatment contrast.

In 204 people with early Parkinson’s, sarcopenic obesity was associated with lower MoCA (p .033) and not with NMSS or SCOPA-AUT. Body composition defines the comparison. No dietary intervention or food contrast.
Narrative micro- and nanoplastics review. The exposure pathway schematic and original biomonitoring citations do not test named foods against Parkinson symptoms.

Eclipta prostrata-derived silver nanoparticles changed wire hang, oral movements and hole-board behavior in haloperidol-treated rats at the two higher doses. No plain-extract or silver-only arm. Earlier plain-leaf extracts are distinct preclinical studies.
Matches the 2025 Armenian rotenone study, PMID 40952533, using intraperitoneal curcumin and catalepsy/rearing outcomes. Already cataloged. No whole turmeric or measured human symptom endpoint.

NCT07567794 specifies diet questionnaires or diaries at baseline and months 12/24. The registry, 2025 ANMS abstract and supplement do not identify the instrument or foods, and the registry has no outcomes.
Optical subthalamic eOPN3 intervention in a 6-OHDA model measured locomotion. No dietary exposure.

The PPMI solvent preprint and poster use weekly caffeinated-drink frequency as a background variable. No beverage-specific or caffeine-to-symptom model. Depression and UPDRS are group characteristics.

Cheese and dried fruit appear in an MSA genetic analysis. Abdominal pain is separate, with no food-by-pain comparison. The earlier idiopathic Parkinson dried-fruit genetic analysis estimates disease odds and is already cataloged.
Bilateral STN DBS in 25 people with Parkinson disease measured motor outcomes and impulsive-compulsive behaviors. No food exposure.
Y7 rat motor and circulating levodopa work overlaps the 37033 abstract and US20260102444A1 study family. No individual culinary fermented food or completed human outcomes.
Cortical protein proximity signal in seven Parkinson cases and five controls. No dietary exposure or food-to-symptom comparison.

disposition: other disease fly model with related plant lead
assessment: Pueraria tuberosa extract in fly feed yielded a small high-dose crawling change in a Friedreich ataxia model. A separate 2022 tuber-extract study reports motor outcomes in haloperidol-treated rats.
Levodopa-induced movements and striatal dopamine photometry in 6-OHDA mice. No botanical or culinary exposure.
The review estimates restless legs syndrome prevalence and compares clinical and diagnostic profiles. It reports no food exposure or intake-specific symptom estimate.
Dysphagia and other symptoms are adverse-event reports from an opicapone database. The abstract contains no food contrast. Earlier healthy-volunteer studies compared fed and fasted drug exposure.
The patient with an ATXN2 expansion denied dysphagia. Parkinson disease appears in the family history and no food exposure is described.
Dysphagia occurs in a patient with SCA27B and a probable MSA-C phenotype. The comparison concerns diagnostic findings and medication response without a food test.
Fiber denotes anatomical connections in DBS tractography. The study is a Huntington disease stimulation case series.
SAGE Publications occurs in a cited reference. Fatigue is characterized by imaging and gene expression without sage exposure.
Dysphagia occurs in an autoimmune overlap case treated with immune and antispasmodic drugs. No food comparison or Parkinson diagnosis appears.
The essential tremor trial measures eating-related activity as an outcome of ulixacaltamide. It does not assign a food exposure.
A paraneoplastic case reports dysphagia changing after immune and symptomatic treatment. No food exposure or Parkinson diagnosis was reported.

MDS 209 reports dysphagia requiring nasogastric feeding during acute encephalitic parkinsonism. It reports motor recovery after treatment of encephalitis, with no formula, ingredient, solid bolus, or food-specific outcome.

MDS 404 pooled three studies of daxibotulinumtoxinA injections for cervical dystonia. Dysphagia was reported in 3%. It concerns an injection adverse event and provides no dietary exposure or idiopathic Parkinson comparison.

MDS 286 reports genetically confirmed neuronal intranuclear inclusion disease with vomiting, aspiration pneumonia, severe gastroparesis and feeding jejunostomy. No dietary ingredient, formula or identified aspirated food is reported.

MDS 1824 reviews 78 Cardiff sialorrhea clinic patients with Parkinson's. Outcomes are drooling, botulinum treatment and survival. Dysphagia is cited as a prognostic context without an itemized food or swallowing test.

MDS 1304 reports 14/58 de novo Parkinson participants with dysphagia on a dichotomized UPDRS item. It measures symptom associations with speech and gait, with no named bolus, tested food, or food-specific response.

MDS 116 delivered five education sessions, including speech and swallowing, to 25 people with PSP and 25 caregivers. Six-month measures concern satisfaction, care experience, caregiver burden and quality of life. No named food intervention or measured swallowing endpoint appears in the abstract.

MDS 1812 and its attached Table 2 and figure summarize interviews with 43 people with Parkinson's and 32 caregivers in Cebu. The September 4 journal abstract (PMID 42696107, DOI 10.1007/s00702-026-03270-5) reports the same sample and updated ages. Available abstract and figures name no food, bolus, or food-specific symptom outcome.

MDS 1606 describes advanced Parkinson's with PEG feeding, acute colonic pseudo-obstruction, and aspiration pneumonia. The authors report stopping PEG feeds during bowel rest, without identifying formula or aspirate or attributing a symptom to a named ingredient.

MDS 99 discusses nutrition and hydration as examples of life-sustaining measures in an ethical and comparative legal analysis. It reports no patient intervention, measured food exposure or symptom outcome.

MDS 1849 measures referral volume and time to specialist review. Dysphagia is named as an inpatient risk, and both attached figures show review pathway results. The study reports no tested food or measured swallowing outcome.

MDS 358 measures tremor distribution and severity in 57 oromandibular dystonia cases. Mastication is background context. The cohort reports no named food, swallowing outcome, or idiopathic Parkinson analysis.

MDS 150 validates a Chinese multiple system atrophy rating scale in TALISMAN (NCT05453058). Adaptation of a food-cutting item and floor effects on a swallowing item concern scale properties, with no named food exposure or food-specific result.

MDS 1474 likely IMPACT 360 NCT07443293. Six-month MIND diet, exercise and mindfulness, 13 paired imaging datasets. No results survived false-discovery correction. Registry lists planned motor and nonmotor outcomes and no posted results. See research/2025-2029/Food-Experiment-MDS-Diet-Followup.md#impact-360-multimodal-lifestyle-and-brain-imaging.

MDS 975 and April 2026 PMID42001670 use 148 iRBD and 142 controls. Later abstract reports 35 conversions vs 34 in the paper. Table 1 shows separate alcohol history by diagnosis (30.6% vs 28.7%, p .722), no alcohol-by-RBD severity estimate. Table 3 associations are serum markers and dementia conversion. See research/2025-2029/Food-Experiment-MDS-Diet-Followup.md#serum-biomarkers-and-phenoconversion-in-beijing.

MDS 1636. Coffee (p .025), alcohol (p .004) and sleep habits are separately compared in 131 Parkinson and 131 matched controls. Related 2024 and 2026 full texts have matching enrollment counts and shared ethics approval but no beverage measure. No coffee preparation or beverage-by-symptom estimate. See research/2025-2029/Food-Experiment-MDS-Beverage-Followup.md#coffee-habits-and-sleep-questionnaire-in-a-romanian-case-control-study.

Plants for Parkinson 236-person trial plans six months of coached plant-based whole-food diet and six months of follow-up. Co-primary MDS-UPDRS III and Wexner constipation. Results blank, protocol and discrepancies with P26.02 already cataloged at research/2025-2029/Food-Experiment-WHO-ICTRP-Followup.md#plants-for-parkinson.

MDS 805 Suhendro extraction table already audited. Six studies include capsules, sachets, liquid probiotic and fecal microbiota transplant. Relevant primary results are in research/2025-2029/Food-Experiment-MDS-Diet-Followup.md#probiotic-capsule-trial-with-measured-rem-sleep-behavior-symptoms. No single culinary food exposure.

Forty-three Parkinson patients. Serum vitamin D averaged 18.5 versus 16.7 ng/mL across good and reduced or absent levodopa-response groups, with no significant difference. No consumed food or assigned vitamin intervention and no separate gastrointestinal estimate in abstract.

53-person two-year Parkinson cohort. Changes in weight and BMI had no significant reported association with change in motor scores, Hoehn and Yahr stage, or levodopa-equivalent dose. No food or nutrition intervention.
Older adults with diabetes, prediabetes or normoglycemia, with prior neurodegenerative diagnoses excluded. Gait and MRI associations with serum markers are outside the Parkinson dietary question.
124 adolescents with type 1 diabetes and dystonia. Relates serum nutritional biomarkers to symptom severity without a dietary intervention or idiopathic Parkinson’s population.
